teaching_point: Palpable purpura with haemorrhagic papules on the ankle — "palpable purpura is vasculitis until proven otherwise". Dipstick the urine and check BP today.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Haemorrhagic vesicles/necrotic papules in leukocytoclastic vasculitis — necrosis/ulceration = more severe; same-day/urgent specialist input.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Hypersensitivity (drug-induced) vasculitis — symmetrical petechiae/purpura on both lower legs.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hypersensitivity vasculitis (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-small-vessel-vasculitis

teaching_point: Dependent-site vasculitis with pustular/necrotic centres — gravity and venous stasis favour immune-complex deposition in the legs.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Purpura on feet and toes — check pulses and cold sensitivity (cryoglobulins), and consider septic emboli if febrile.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Vasculitic purpura on the feet/ankles — non-blanching on diascopy; distinguish from flat thrombocytopenic petechiae.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Vasculitis (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/purpura

teaching_point: Osler nodes — tender red-purple nodules on finger pads/dorsum (immunological phenomenon, usually subacute endocarditis). Not pathognomonic (also SLE, gonococcaemia).
dermnet_caption: Osler node on ring finger as well as more subtle nodes seen on the little and middle finger
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Osler node on ring finger as well as more subtle nodes seen on the little and middle finger (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/osler-nodes-and-janeway-lesions

teaching_point: Osler node on the index finger with tiny splinter haemorrhages — combine skin signs with fever, murmur and blood cultures (modified Duke minor criteria).
dermnet_caption: Osler nodes on index finger. Note also the tiny splinter haemorrhages on fingernail also seen in end
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Osler nodes on index finger. Note also the tiny splinter haemorrhages on fingernail also seen in end (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/osler-nodes-and-janeway-lesions

teaching_point: Splinter haemorrhages — longitudinal dark lines in the nail bed; most are traumatic (distal). Suspicious if multiple, proximal, new, or with systemic features.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Several splinter haemorrhages in one nail — number alone does not diagnose endocarditis; context does.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Splinter haemorrhages in psoriatic nail dystrophy — common benign cause (also onychomycosis, manual work).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Septic emboli on the sole — painless haemorrhagic macules on soles/palms are the Janeway-lesion pattern (vascular phenomenon, acute S. aureus endocarditis). Same-day admission.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Urticarial vasculitis on the leg — wheal-like plaques lasting >24 h, burning/tender rather than itchy, leaving bruising/pigment.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Urticarial vasculitis with residual purpura/dusky staining — the "leaves a mark" clue that separates UV from ordinary urticaria.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Cutaneous PAN — tender subcutaneous nodules along the leg with livedo (medium-vessel vasculitis at the dermal–subcutaneous junction).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-polyarteritis-nodosa

teaching_point: Punched-out ulcers in PAN; deep (incisional) biopsy needed to sample medium vessels.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-polyarteritis-nodosa

teaching_point: Livedo reticularis — regular, complete violaceous net. Physiological if it fades on warming.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Livedo racemosa — irregular, broken rings that persist when warm: think PAN, antiphospholipid syndrome/Sneddon, SLE, cholesterol emboli.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Cutis marmorata — physiological cold-induced mottling (infants, young women) that resolves with rewarming — the benign end of the livedo spectrum.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Atrophie blanche / livedoid vasculopathy — painful ankle ulcers healing with white stellate scars; occlusive (thrombotic), not vasculitic; DDx for ulcerating livedo.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: IgA vasculitis (HSP) — palpable purpura on the ankle/foot, the classic dependent distribution.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Ankle swelling/arthritis in IgA vasculitis — joint involvement in ~75%; paracetamol for pain.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Buttock and leg purpura — classic dependent/extensor distribution of IgA vasculitis. Monitor urine and BP for at least 6 months.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Acute haemorrhagic oedema of infancy — large rosette/target purpuric plaques with oedema in a well infant (4 months–2 years).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acute haemorrhagic oedema (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acute-haemorrhagic-oedema-of-infancy

teaching_point: Cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis — purpura on the legs (± ulcers, livedo, acral necrosis, arthralgia); check hepatitis C.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Lip ulceration in granulomatosis with polyangiitis (c-ANCA/PR3) — ENT, lung and kidney disease; rare in children.
dermnet_caption: Lip ulceration due to granulomatosis with polyangiitis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lip ulceration due to granulomatosis with polyangiitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/granulomatosis-with-polyangiitis

teaching_point: Purpura in disseminated intravascular coagulation — the "unwell + purpura" emergency (meningococcal sepsis) that must be excluded before labelling a child's rash as HSP.
